objective: Standard statement: for each of the 16 classes of three-bit relations with every two coordinates unconstrained (up to coordinate order), find the hub gadgets of at most six copies of the relation whose projection onto the legs is a coordinate permutation of it and gives every allowed leg tuple the same number of extensions (the factor); record the smallest size, the factors and, for gadgets with all three leg pairs at one distance s, the similarity dimension log(copies)/log(s) of the tower. Prove the factor formula (factor = number of solutions of the gadget with free legs divided by the size of the relation) and a sufficient condition (a group of gadget automorphisms with value symmetries of the relation acting transitively on its tuples). Nearest known result: HUB-SURVIVORS-20261029-001 (which classes are rebuilt; not-all-equal exact on the Fano plane); exact renormalization on hierarchical and fractal lattices. Classification: no overlap found (candidate local delta).
status: Proved by EXACT-TOWERS-20261029-001A-P001 (V1, prose plus exhaustive census): an exact counted fixed point rebuilds its knot with the same number c of hidden completions for every allowed leg tuple; c is the free solution count over |K|; every parity rebuild is exact (affine fibres) and transitive automorphisms force exactness (possible only for parity, not-all-equal and twisted not-all-equal). Up to six copies exact gadgets exist exactly for parity (from three), twisted not-all-equal (from four) and the two three-excluded classes (from five); x or (y != z) is rebuilt but never exact; not-all-equal is exact at seven (Fano, factor 5). Mechanisms: pendant, frozen hidden variable, tied pair or transitive automorphisms, except 22 gadgets at six copies. Smallest single-scale growth exponents: log2 3, 2, log2 6, log3 7.
title: Exact counted fixed points: which knots, at which sizes, with which factors
